solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Acquire case of Sauterne — it's restorative!

indicators.note: the case of a word is its outside, so only the first and last letters of the wine are kept

parts.note: a restorative is a cure, something that puts you right

explanation.surface: A wine lover claims a bottle of Sauterne will set them back on their feet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Restorative!' looks like the definition, but it is a noun giving CURE; the definition is 'Acquire' at the front.
explanation.definitionFit: To secure something is to obtain or get hold of it, a plain synonym.

clue.text: Conceal empty suitcase on island

indicators.note: an empty suitcase has nothing inside, so only the outer letters of the word stay

parts.note: Crete is the large Greek island

explanation.surface: A smuggler hides an empty suitcase somewhere on a Greek island.
explanation.definitionFit: To secrete something is to hide it away, a less common sense than producing a fluid.

clue.text: Very many are of inferior significance

definitions.meaning: too numerous to be tallied, innumerable
read as two words, matter less or carry less weight

explanation.surface: A grumble that numerous things are of little importance.
explanation.definitionFit: Innumerable things cannot be tallied; split in two, the phrase means to matter less.

clue.text: Errors fairly regularly found in prayers

indicators.note: regularly means taking every second letter of the words before it

explanation.surface: Mistakes crop up quite often in people's prayers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fairly' belongs to the letters picked from, not to the indicator: the even letters of ERRORS FAIRLY are taken.
explanation.definitionFit: A rosary is a set series of Catholic prayers counted on beads.

clue.text: Husband in Bermuda whirled and danced

indicators.note: in places the abbreviation for husband inside the rearranged island name
whirled suggests spinning round, so the letters of the island are jumbled

explanation.surface: A husband spun round the dance floor on holiday in Bermuda.
explanation.walkthrough: 'whirled' turns BERMUDA into RUMBAED, and 'in' puts H inside it after the R.
explanation.definitionFit: To rhumba is to dance the Cuban ballroom dance, so the past tense means did that dance.

clue.text: Tail of skittish wildebeest lifted and dropped

indicators.note: the tail of a word is its final letter
in a down clue, lifted means the word is read upwards, so backwards

parts.note: a gnu is another name for a wildebeest

explanation.surface: A nervous wildebeest raises and lowers its tail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lifted and dropped' reads as one action, but 'lifted' signals the upward reading and 'dropped' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A head that is hung has been lowered, as in hanging one's head in shame.

clue.text: People add up in their heads

parts.note: men means people in general, as in all men
to tally is to count up or total

explanation.surface: People doing mental arithmetic rather than using a calculator.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something mentally means doing it inside one's mind, an adverb phrase matching the adverb.

clue.text: Feet of Mahatma Gandhi removing skin from solid mayonnaise

indicators.note: the feet of words in a down clue are their bottom, final letters
taking the skin off a word strips its outside letters, leaving the inside

explanation.surface: Gandhi's feet and solid mayonnaise make an odd picture of skin care.
explanation.definitionFit: Aioli is a garlic-flavoured mayonnaise from Provence.

clue.text: Vandalises Home Counties eaterie and departs northwards

indicators.note: in a down clue, going northwards means reading upwards, so the whole string is turned round

parts.note: SE, the South East of England, stands for the Home Counties around London
a cafe is a small eaterie
D is the timetable abbreviation for departs

explanation.surface: Someone trashes a cafe in the commuter belt and runs off north.
explanation.walkthrough: 'northwards' turns SECAFED round. The Home Counties are the counties surrounding London.
explanation.definitionFit: To deface something is to spoil its surface, a form of vandalism.

clue.text: Old dons swear in classes

indicators.note: dons means puts on or takes in, here read as the swear word taking in the letter for old

parts.note: to curse is to swear

explanation.surface: Elderly university lecturers swearing during their teaching sessions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dons' looks like university teachers but is the container: O goes inside CURSE.
explanation.definitionFit: A course is a series of lessons, so it can mean classes.

clue.text: Seedsman with shed, but not all the time

parts.note: Onan, in Genesis, spilled his seed on the ground, hence a jokey seedsman
to doff is to take off or shed, as a hat is doffed

explanation.surface: A gardener and his garden shed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Seedsman' looks like a nursery trader; it is the Old Testament figure ONAN.
explanation.definitionFit: Something done intermittently happens at intervals rather than continuously.

clue.text: Japanese scoff and point when male is half-cut

parts.note: S, south, is a compass point
as means when, as in as I left
him is a male pronoun

indicators.note: half-cut means only the first half of the little word is kept

explanation.surface: A tipsy man tucks into Japanese food and points at things.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half-cut' looks like drunk, but it halves IS to its first letter. 'Scoff' is British slang for food.
explanation.definitionFit: Sashimi is a Japanese dish of thinly sliced raw fish, and scoff is slang for food.

clue.text: Superficial old bird, vacuously amoral

parts.note: ex means former or old, as in ex-wife
a tern is a seabird

indicators.note: vacuously means emptied, so the inside of the word goes and its ends stay

explanation.surface: A description of a shallow, empty-headed old flame.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bird' is British slang for a girlfriend, hinting at a person, but it is the seabird.
explanation.definitionFit: External and superficial both describe what is on the outer surface only.

clue.text: Am about to invent reverse- operating staple!

indicators.note: about means turned around, so the little word is read backwards

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: reverse-operating means working backwards, so the word for invent is written in reverse

parts.note: to coin a word is to invent it

explanation.surface: Someone about to invent a machine that runs backwards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' turns AM to MA, and 'reverse-operating' turns COIN to NIOC.
explanation.definitionFit: Manioc, or cassava, is a starchy root that is a staple food across the tropics.

clue.text: Name for large, foolish bystander

indicators.note: for means in place of, so one letter is swapped for another

parts.note: witless means foolish, lacking sense
L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large

explanation.surface: Naming a big, silly onlooker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Name for large' puts N in place of the L in WITLESS.
explanation.definitionFit: A witness is someone who sees an event, an onlooker.

clue.text: Jug used to be back to front

indicators.note: the back letter of the phrase is moved round to its front

parts.note: were is the past of be, what things used to be

explanation.surface: An object that was once the wrong way round.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back to front' moves the final E of WERE to the start rather than turning the word round.
explanation.definitionFit: A ewer is a large wide-mouthed jug, once used with a washing bowl.

clue.text: Charles, accepting I flirt outrageously, means to get high

indicators.note: accepting means taking in, so the short name holds the other letters
outrageously means wildly, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Charles lets someone flirt with him shamelessly to get his kicks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outrageously' turns I FLIRT into AIRLIFT, which goes inside CH..S.
explanation.definitionFit: Chairlifts carry skiers up mountains, so they are ways of getting up high.

clue.text: Filmed us raging over a medieval social system

indicators.note: raging means wild, so the letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: A film crew caught someone furious about the Middle Ages.
explanation.definitionFit: Feudalism was the medieval order of lords, vassals and serfs bound by land and service.

clue.text: Iron short skirt and submit, content to be invisible? Not she!

definitions.note: a cryptic pointer to a woman who would refuse to iron, wear a mini and submit

parts.note: Fe is the chemical symbol for iron
a mini is a short skirt

indicators.note: with its content invisible, only the outer letters of the word show

explanation.surface: A list of domestic, compliant behaviour that a certain kind of woman would reject.
explanation.walkthrough: 'content to be invisible' looks like meek self-effacement, but it empties SUBMIT to ST.
explanation.definitionFit: A campaigner for women's rights would reject ironing, short skirts and submission.

clue.text: Einstein taking part in Michaelmas term indiscretions

indicators.note: taking part in says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A genius getting up to mischief during the autumn term at Oxford or Cambridge.
explanation.walkthrough: Michaelmas term is the autumn term at Oxford and Cambridge.
explanation.definitionFit: Einstein is used generically for a genius, a brilliant planner or intellect.

clue.text: Mum and kid close to extraordinary grandeur

parts.note: ma is an informal word for mum
to kid is to joke, or jest

indicators.note: the close of a word is its last letter

explanation.surface: A mother and child near something extraordinary and grand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'kid' looks like a child beside 'Mum', but it is the verb meaning tease.
explanation.definitionFit: Majesty means stately splendour or dignity.

clue.text: Dowdy woman initially left behind

indicators.note: the initial letter is left off the word for the woman

parts.note: a frump is a dowdy, unfashionable woman

explanation.surface: A plain woman was abandoned at the start.
explanation.walkthrough: 'left behind' reads as one phrase; split it: 'initially left' drops the F and 'behind' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Behind and rump both mean the buttocks or backside.

clue.text: Back entrance of post office not yielding

parts.note: stern means firm and unbending

explanation.surface: A rear door at a post office that won't budge.
explanation.definitionFit: A postern is a back or side gate, especially in a castle wall.

clue.text: High-class crack and dope served up, in an ideal world

parts.note: U stands for upper-class, high-class

indicators.note: in a down clue, served up means read upwards, so the pair is written backwards

parts.note: A1 means crack, first-rate, with 1 read as I
pot is slang for cannabis, dope

explanation.surface: Posh drug users dream of paradise while being served crack and dope.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crack' and 'dope' look like drugs; 'crack' means excellent, A1. 'served up' turns A1POT round to TOP1A.
explanation.definitionFit: Utopia is an imagined perfect society, from Thomas More's book.

clue.text: Idiot wearing jacket

parts.note: a jerk is a fool
in means wearing, as in in a suit

explanation.surface: A fool dressed in a jacket.
explanation.definitionFit: A jerkin is a close-fitting sleeveless jacket.

clue.text: Reminder of immature licentiousness

indicators.note: of here means made out of, part of, the letters of the words that follow

explanation.surface: A memento of youthful debauchery.
explanation.definitionFit: A relic is an object surviving from the past that serves as a memento.

clue.text: Satyr has massaged butts in these

indicators.note: massaged means worked over or manipulated, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A lecherous satyr has had his bottom rubbed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'butts' looks like bottoms, but means cigarette ends.
explanation.definitionFit: Ashtrays are receptacles that cigarette ends are stubbed out in.

clue.text: Smile broadly and run into trap

indicators.note: into places the abbreviation for run inside the word for trap

parts.note: a gin is a snare or trap
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: Someone beams and then blunders into a snare.
explanation.definitionFit: To grin is to smile widely, showing the teeth.

clue.text: Armed forces very direly mistreated

parts.note: so means very, as in so good

indicators.note: mistreated means handled badly, so the letters are knocked out of order

explanation.surface: Troops treated appallingly badly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'very' is not part of the fodder as printed: it gives SO, which joins DIRELY to make the letters rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Soldiery is a collective word for soldiers, a body of troops.

clue.text: Super 8 is then periodically ditched for Brownie

indicators.note: every other character is ditched at regular intervals, keeping the rest

explanation.surface: A Brownie swaps her cine camera for something else.
explanation.walkthrough: The figure 8 counts as a character to be dropped. A Brownie is a helpful household elf in folklore, not a young Girl Guide here.
explanation.definitionFit: A brownie is a small helpful goblin of folklore, a kind of elf.

clue.text: Cynthia playing golf, an expensive hobby

indicators.note: playing suggests the letters are messed about with, so they are rearranged

parts.note: G is golf in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Cynthia takes up golf, a costly pastime.
explanation.definitionFit: Sailing pleasure boats is a famously costly leisure pursuit.

clue.text: Black hole in wall starts to alarm nervous attendant

parts.note: B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils
hole in the wall is British slang for a cash machine, an ATM

indicators.note: the starts of the words are their first letters

explanation.surface: A dark hole in a wall begins to worry an anxious servant.
explanation.walkthrough: A hole in the wall is the everyday British name for a cash machine.
explanation.definitionFit: A batman is an army officer's personal servant.
